mappings.note: The Khyber Pass: what terrain it is, and what it offered or cost an army and a caravan. CG-SST1 for the terrain reading, since LO-48 asks how landforms form and this asks what a pass affords; LO-55 for the military use of a corridor. (Answer is a watermark line plus a stray fragment; see report.)
Building a 'star of dynasties' for this chapter's powers. Mapping the kingdoms of the period, LO-55. (Empty answer on this row; see report.)
Drawing a geographical tour of the chapter's dynasties on a subcontinent map. CG-SST1 for the map work (LO-50 being climatic regions only), LO-55 for the dynasties being located.
Calculating the distance Rajendra I's fleet sailed to Srivijaya. CG-SST1 for measuring on a map, LO-55 for the naval expedition itself. (Answer runs on into unrelated text; see report.)

Basavanna's anubhava mandapa opening debate to all backgrounds, and what it teaches about a just society now. LO-58 for the reform movement challenging caste and ritual; LO-60 because parts (b) and (c) ask what equality demands of a civil society today.

Al-Biruni praising the extinguished Hindu Shahiya house from inside Mahmud's entourage. CG-SST2 for weighing a hostile-side source, LO-56 because the exercise is to judge one ruling house against its conqueror.
Why the period counts as a transition, with two examples each of change and continuity. Periodisation and historical judgement; goal-level CG-SST2, as no LO covers it.

The Somanatha temple rebuilt in 1950 entirely on public donation, and why that was chosen. LO-57 for the temple and its repeated rebuilding, CG-SST2 for reading a modern act as a statement about the past.

Reading a painting to tell king from guru and interpreting Rajendra Chola's anjali mudra and bowed head. Working from a visual source, goal-level CG-SST2; LO-57 is rejected because nothing architectural is at issue.

Juzjani's Tabakat-i-Nasiri calling a captured 'fortress' a college, and finding clues that it was Nalanda Mahavihara. The chapter's clearest source-criticism exercise; goal-level CG-SST2, since CG-SST2's competencies do not reach historiography.
Matches Eastern Gangas to Konark, Chandellas to Kandariya Mahadeva, Paramaras to Bhojeshwar, Hoysalas to Belur and Cholas to Brihadishvara. Temple building by dynasty, LO-57.

Tabulating which dynasties persist, vanish or appear between the two chapters. LO-55 for the kingdoms themselves, CG-SST2 for the continuity-and-change judgement; LO-56 is rejected because no ruler's policy is compared.
Why centres of learning such as Nalanda mattered, and the cost of their destruction. Intellectual history of the period, goal-level CG-SST2. (Empty answer on this row; see report.)

Mahmud raiding for plunder against Ghuri seeking territory, and how the difference shaped each campaign's outcome. A direct LO-56 fit - comparing the policies of two rulers - rather than LO-55, which would stop at the campaigns themselves.
Why the 11th and 12th centuries are transitional: Turkic invasions reshaping power and introducing Islamic rule. Periodisation, goal-level CG-SST2, matching the other transition item.
'Sultan' as an Arabic term for authority, used for a sovereign ruler. Vocabulary of rulership, LO-55; CG-SST2 is reserved here for source and periodisation items.
Al-Biruni's observation that Indian sciences and scholars moved to Kashmir and Varanasi after Mahmud's ruin of the conquered regions. A testimony about intellectual life, goal-level CG-SST2.
Hoysala star-shaped plans and intricately carved stone. Distinctive temple style and technique, LO-57 exactly.
Rajendra Chola I's naval strike at Srivijaya to command the Malacca route to China. Strategy for control, LO-55.

Mularaja II and Queen Naikidevi turning back Muhammad Ghuri at Mount Abu in 1178. LO-55 for the engagement; LO-66 for the queen's part in it, that being the frame's only women-focused outcome even though it is framed around disadvantage.
The Second Battle of Tarain, 1192, opening Delhi and the Ganga plains to Turkic rule. Military outcome, LO-55.
Ramanuja's vishishtadvaita holding world and souls real against Shankara's advaita. A new religious-philosophical position, LO-58; LO-59 is rejected as it concerns bhakti and sufi verse.
The anubhava mandapa as an open forum for all backgrounds. Same pair as the long-form item: LO-58 for the reform movement, LO-60 because the answer rests on its inclusiveness.
Mobile cavalry and mounted archers outmanoeuvring elephant-heavy Indian armies. Military strategy, LO-55.
Ghuri striking coins with the Lakshmi motif to legitimise his rule and ease trade. Coinage as an instrument of authority, LO-55.
'Turkic' as an ethnolinguistic term spanning Central Asia to Siberia, not a modern nationality. Historical terminology, goal-level CG-SST2.

Vachanas as short Kannada poems carrying Basaveshvara's ethical vision and devotion. LO-59 is a direct fit - drawing meaning from bhakti poetry - as against LO-58, which covers why the movement arose.
Why the era is not a 'historical void': regional literature, temple building, bhakti and trade. A judgement about a period's character, goal-level CG-SST2.

Assertion-reason rejecting the claim that Chola-Srivijaya relations were purely hostile, given a Srivijaya-funded monastery at Nalanda. LO-55 for the expedition, CG-SST2 for the wider cultural relationship the reason evidences.
Paramaras rising from vassals to an independent Malwa power at Dhara. Kingdom and seat, LO-55.
Bhoja Paramara, scholar-king, founder of Bhojpur and builder of a great lake. Ruler identification, LO-55; the option set turns on telling him from the Pratihara Bhoja.
The Samarangana Sutradhara on architecture, town planning, sculpture and mechanical devices, but not naval warfare. A treatise on building, LO-57.
Ajayameru (Ajmer) as the Chahamana capital under Prithviraja III, distinguished from the Delhi they also held. Seat of a kingdom, LO-55.
Qutb-ud-din Aibak left to consolidate Ghuri's conquests and founding the Delhi Sultanate. Military and administrative succession, LO-55.

Mapped on its stem, which asks which Ghurid commander destroyed Nalanda and Vikramashila - a military campaign, LO-55. (The options and answer stored on this row belong to a different question, about Jayadeva and the Gitagovindam; see report.)
Eastern Gangas initiating the Konark Sun temple, having built at Puri. Temple construction by dynasty, LO-57.

Kakatiyas ruling from Warangal and building the Thousand Pillar temple, against the false claim that the Cholas absorbed them. LO-55 for the kingdom's fortunes, LO-57 for the temple. (Stem survives only as its last line; see report.)
'Poy, Sala' - 'Strike, Sala' - as the legend behind the Hoysala name. Dynastic origin, LO-55.
Velapura (Belur) and Dvarasamudra (Halebidu) as the Hoysala capitals. Seats of a kingdom, LO-55; LO-57 is rejected because the temples there are not what is asked.
Rajaraja Chola I taking northern Sri Lanka and the 'islands of the sea' around 1000 CE. Military expansion, LO-55.
Rajaraja Chola I as builder of the Brihadishvara at Thanjavur. The temple is what is being recalled, so LO-57 rather than LO-55.
Mahmud of Ghazni defeating the Hindu Shahis Jayapala and Anandapala. Military strategy, LO-55.
Mahmud's seventeen campaigns into India. Scale of a raiding strategy, LO-55; LO-56 is reserved for the item that sets his motive against Ghuri's.
The 1026 attack on Somanatha and its plunder. The raid is what is tested, so LO-55; the Somanatha rebuilding item carries LO-57 instead, which is the difference between them.
Al-Biruni learning Sanskrit and compiling an encyclopaedic survey of Indian religion, philosophy and science. A major source and its making, goal-level CG-SST2.
Al-Biruni's Arabic translation of Patanjali's Yogasutras. Transmission of texts across cultures, goal-level CG-SST2.
Bhaskaracharya's Lilavati and Bijaganita. History of science, goal-level CG-SST2.
Senas succeeding the Palas in Bengal from Nadiya. Dynastic succession and capital, LO-55.

Mapped on its stem, which asks for the Gitagovindam's author under Sena patronage - Jayadeva's devotional poetry, LO-59. (The key and explanation stored on this row are Bakhtiyar Khilji's, transposed with another item; see report.)
Someshvara III's Manasollasa, an encyclopaedia of royal life and governance. LO-55 for its subject - how a kingdom is run - and CG-SST2 for the text as a source.
Chandella temples at Khajuraho, Kandariya Mahadeva and Lakshmana. Temple construction by dynasty, LO-57.
Basaveshvara leaving office to found the Lingayat movement. The emergence of a new religious movement, LO-58; LO-59 is kept for the vachanas themselves.
Angkor Wat built by Suryavarman II for Vishnu. Temple identification and dedication, LO-57.

Angkor Wat as the largest religious monument with towers evoking Mount Meru, against the false claim of destruction. Temple design and symbolism, LO-57. (Stem survives only as its last line; see report.)
Suheldev defeating Salar Masud at Bahraich. Local military resistance, LO-55.
Qutb-ud-din Aibak as the Ghurid general who founded the Delhi Sultanate. Dynastic and military recall, LO-55.
Nalanda as the university Bakhtiyar Khilji destroyed. A campaign's target, LO-55; CG-SST2 is reserved for the Juzjani source item that reconstructs the same event from a text.
Suheldev as the ruler who resisted Salar Masud. Military resistance, LO-55.
Delhi as Dhillika under the Chahamanas. A kingdom's city and its historical name, LO-55.
Al-Biruni as translator of the Yogasutras into Arabic. Transmission of texts, goal-level CG-SST2.
